items.summary: Anthropic, an AI firm valued at US$1 trillion (S$1. 3 trillion), is pursuing a stock market debut after five years of rapid growth. In its Oct 26 prospectus it warns that model differentiation may narrow, with substantially all revenue from AI tools and no advertising or cloud business to fall back on. Shareholders had floated a valuation of US$2 trillion but slowed quarter-on-quarter growth from 145% in the second quarter to 45% in the third, cooling expectations to around US$1. 5 trillion. The article identifies three threats: commoditisation as open models such as Kimi K3. 1 Pro close behind paid ones like Claude Opus 5.
items.title: Anthropic’s record IPO faces three threats as rivals catch up and prices fall

items.summary: Paris Smaragdis, an MIT professor with joint appointments in the Music and Theatre Arts program, Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, and the Schwarzman College of Computing, researches machine learning for sound perception. He aims to help machines hear and understand audio as well as humans do, citing applications like locating traffic accidents by tire sounds or detecting drill failures underground. Smaragdis joined MIT in 2025 after a career at Mitsubishi Electric Research Labs, Adobe, and the University of Illinois. His group focuses on tools for musicians and flexible signal processing techniques.
items.title: MIT Professor Paris Smaragdis Advances Machine Hearing Research

items.summary: Reliance’s Jio Platforms shares rose 21% in their Mumbai debut on Oct 28, giving India’s biggest-ever initial public offering a strong start and making it the second-largest company by market capitalisation in India at about US$131.52 billion (S$168.6 billion), ahead of Bharti Airtel and HDFC Bank. The listing marks Reliance Industries’ first sale after two decades, as Ambani pursues an “everything company” strategy across consumer and technology sectors.
items.title: Jio Platforms Shares Jump After Record Indian IPO Debut

items.summary: The Australian federal government has advanced a digital duty of care bill through the House of Representatives, aiming for passage by end 2026. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese framed it around children treating chatbots as their best friend and urged the Coalition to support it. The Greens back the law; the Coalition opposes it while Labor seeks its backing amid possible amendments. Accepted changes would ban AI conduct simulating emotional intimacy that fosters a child's dependence on it, requiring platforms to offer algorithm opt-outs. Communications minister Anika Wells rejected claims of censorship as an Orwellian slogan. The bill now moves to the Senate, where Greens and independent MPs push for external complaints mechanisms and expanded powers for the telecommunications industry ombudsman.
items.title: Australia's digital duty of care bill would ban AI emotional intimacy

items.summary: Tech Life, a BBC World Service programme presented by Chris Vallance and produced by Imran Rahman-Jones, previews its next episodes. It tells the story of the PHP crisis after vulnerabilities were discovered that made the acronym widely known. The show also features an interview with a comedian whose jokes were retold by an AI avatar that gained millions of views online, plus questions answered by the director of the UK's national supercomputer following an earlier visit.
items.title: BBC Tech Life programme covers PHP crisis and AI story

items.summary: At a campaign rally in Lubbock, Texas on Tuesday night, President Donald Trump announced his administration would terminate the Biden-era methane regulations. The Environmental Protection Agency proposed relaxing monitoring and emission-control requirements after complaints from the oil and gas industry, which called the rules an economic threat. Environmental groups warn that weaker restrictions will worsen air pollution near operations. Experts note stripper wells produce more than half of the industry's emissions yet account for only 5 percent of output. Darin Schroeder of the Clean Air Task Force said marginal producers are not necessarily marginal polluters, and let them off the hook would significantly impact climate change efforts.
items.title: Trump's EPA rolls back methane rules

items.summary: Next week's gubernatorial elections could shift energy and environmental policy across many states, according to Inside Climate News analysis drawing on election forecasts from Sabato's Crystal Ball at the University of Virginia. Democrats are favored to retain governorships in Arizona, Michigan, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin, while also poised to take control from Republicans in Alaska, Iowa and Ohio. Analysts note that Democratic governors with unified legislative majorities have enacted more ambitious climate laws, as seen when Illinois' JB Pritzker gained a trifecta after his 2018 victory. Experts emphasize the governor's power over utility commissions and appointees can determine energy direction, especially amid high prices and scrutiny of bills. Wisconsin, Alaska and other closely contested races draw particular attention because winners could reshape commission membership or data center rules. The article notes that party control alone is insufficient where legislatures remain divided or regulators are elected rather than appointed. A quotation from Dylan Reed underscores the governor's central role in state energy policy over utility costs.
items.title: Governor Races Could Reshape State Energy Policy

items.summary: Oil prices rose in early Asian trade as renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia revived supply concerns, with Brent futures at $115.70 per barrel up 1.62% and WTI at $101.20 per barrel up 1.34%. The Houthis claimed a ballistic missile hit the Ras Tanura refinery, though Saudi authorities have not confirmed damage or operational interruption. Falling inventories estimated by the American Petroleum Institute added support while reports of an impending U.S. campaign against Iran reinforced upward momentum.
items.title: Houthi Strikes on Ras Tanura and U.S. War Rumors Push Oil Higher

items.summary: The Information reported on Tuesday that OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips, citing a person familiar with the matter. The report did not disclose financial terms or other details. Google and OpenAI both declined comment outside regular business hours. The announcement comes as Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet plan up to $600 billion combined this year in AI infrastructure spending amid investor skepticism about returns.
items.title: OpenAI reportedly planning purchase of Google AI chips

items.summary: Apple launched its new 14-inch MacBook Pro with an M6 chip, claiming up to 30% better graphics performance and a 24-hour battery life. The model starts at ₹2,39,900 in India, with pre-orders opening on October 28, 2026.
items.title: Apple Launches MacBook Pro M6 in India

items.summary: Apple introduced its new 14-inch MacBook Pro powered by the M6 chip, part of an upgrade to its professional laptop lineup aimed at demanding workloads such as software development and video editing. The machine keeps the Liquid Retina XDR display but centers on the processor for heavier applications. Apple frames the launch around whether these changes justify the price.
items.title: Apple launches M6 MacBook Pro in India

items.summary: Japan's Nidec may not obtain an auditor's opinion on its securities report by month-end after PwC Japan said the audit would not be completed in time. The Nikkei business daily reported this without citing sources. Nidec will submit internal control documents to the Tokyo Stock Exchange by the deadline while seeking early review of listing maintenance, and it announced plans to sue founder Shigenobu Nagamori and eight former executives over suspected accounting irregularities.
items.title: Nidec May Miss Audit Deadline, Nikkei Reports

items.summary: The Villa Vie Odyssey suspended its years-long world voyage after fuel costs surged. Its operator said monthly cabin fuel prices rose to as much as $8,000 (£6,000) from $1,800. Around 200 passengers were ordered off in Cambodia. The company will spend the next 60 days restructuring and recapitalising, though no outcome is assured.
items.title: Luxury Cruise Ship Suspends Voyage Over Fuel Costs, Stranding Passengers in Cambodia

items.summary: In a Free Press column excerpt, the author frames artificial intelligence hacking risks as a worst-case scenario rather than an expectation. He argues that current systems use varied protections and would likely prove more robust than feared, shifting toward post-quantum methods even at great cost. The columnist notes math breakthroughs may arrive in stages, giving time to adjust.
items.title: Columnist Frames AI Hacking Risks as Worst-Case Scenario, Not Prediction

items.summary: Plaid Cymru ministers want extra cash for Welsh railways and public services ahead of the UK government's Wednesday Budget. Finance Minister Elin Jones asked Chancellor John Healey to treat Wales fairly, requesting £1bn of promised rail funding be brought forward and help with the 2027-28 budget facing a real-term cut. She said Wales had been short-changed for years. Extra spending on devolved services in England could bring additional funds to Wales. Meanwhile, shoppers at Swansea Market cited cost of living as their top concern ahead of the announcement.
items.title: Plaid Cymru demands more funding as UK Budget approaches

items.summary: The government-backed Warm Home Loans scheme launched Tuesday, offering UK households interest-free or low-interest loans of £7,500 to up £35,000 to fund heat pumps, batteries and solar panels with no upfront cost. Energy suppliers British Gas and E.On partnered with lenders to offer the loans directly. The government says installing these technologies could save households up to £550 a year on energy bills. The scheme runs within a £2.7bn five-year budget that Treasury officials plan to cut, reportedly because they consider it a subsidy used mainly by middle-class households.
items.title: UK Warm Home Loans Scheme Launches for Solar and Heat Pump Upgrades

items.summary: The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region's Center for Food Safety decided on Tuesday, October 23, 2026, to suspend imports of poultry meat and products from Lolland Municipality in Denmark and Jackson County in Minnesota, US. The move followed notifications about highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza outbreaks. A CFS spokesperson said the decision protects public health, with trade instructed to stop importing immediately.
items.title: Hong Kong Suspends Poultry Imports Over Avian Flu Outbreaks

items.summary: Israeli exit polls show Benjamin Netanyahu's governing bloc tied with the opposition grouping led by Gadi Eisenkot on 51 seats each, short of the 61 needed to form a majority coalition government. Final counting is ongoing as parties begin negotiations that could take weeks.
items.title: Israel Exit Polls Show Netanyahu and Eisenkot Blocs Tied

items.summary: The National Trust of Australia (Victoria) announced that a ginkgo biloba in Geelong’s botanic gardens won 2026 as Victoria’s tree of the year, beating eight finalists with 27% of 4,435 public votes. Planted in 1859 and standing about 20 metres tall, it is the largest ginkgo in the state and a popular wedding backdrop. National Trust executive manager Justin Buckley called it “a very popular winner” while urging stronger statutory protection for significant trees, which he said remain inadequate. Botanic gardens supervisor Sheree Parker described it as the park’s most visited tree after years of dormancy.
items.title: Geelong ginkgo named Victoria’s tree of the year

items.summary: The 2026 Light of the Internet Expo opens in Wuzhen from November 2 to 5 as part of the World Internet Conference (WIC) Wuzhen Summit. Now in its 12th edition, this year's theme is 'Intelligent Connectivity, Smart Future,' and it will showcase next-generation connectivity, computing, large models, intelligent devices, industry applications, smart living and cybersecurity across six zones. Organizers have prioritized satellite internet, quantum communication, 6G and ultra-wideband.
items.title: Wuzhen Expo Opens With 6G, AI Agents and Robots Focus

items.summary:
Syria reopened its main border crossing with Jordan on Wednesday (Oct 28), as the two countries reaffirmed ties strained by a deadly retaliatory strike from Jordanian forces. The raid followed gunmen opening fire during a Greek Orthodox church funeral in Karak, killing nine people and wounding 25. Syria condemned it an "unacceptable violation," while Jordan said it killed more than 20 militant fighters. A joint security committee will meet to discuss operations against IS. Damascus denied coordinating with Amman over the raids.

items.title: Syria Reopens Jordan Border Crossing After Mending Ties

items.summary: Singer Demi Lovato reassured fans she is 'fine' after sharing a now-deleted Instagram Story showing an IV and hospital wristband. She suggested sushi or passionfruit may have triggered the reaction, writing: "I'm either allergic to passionfruit or sushi now!" A source told TMZ that Lovato was discharged shortly after being evaluated and her symptoms subsided quickly.
items.title: Demi Lovato Reassures Fans After Hospital Visit Over Possible Allergic Reaction

items.summary: Macnica, a Japanese cybersecurity company, reported that cyberattacks on publicly accessible websites and apps have more than doubled from last year, reaching 216 cases of confirmed or suspected data breaches so far this year—about 2.6 times the prior total. A government official said AI was likely being used to make attacks easier.
items.title: Japanese cybersecurity firm reports surge in AI-driven website attacks

items.summary: In Hong Kong, artificial nest boxes are giving the critically endangered yellow-crested cockatoo refuge and research access in a city where storm damage and tree pruning have eliminated more than 60% of natural nesting hollows. Astrid Andersson of the University of Hong Kong calls it “a housing crisis for these birds.” Biologist Harry Wong built camera-fitted boxes with her, installing 15 across parks since March 2025; four are occupied and one chick was successfully raised.
items.title: Nest boxes give Hong Kong’s rare cockatoos shelter amid hollow shortage

items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping extended condolences on Tuesday to the family of former Japanese Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda, who died. Describing him as a statesman known for integrity and responsibility, Xi said Fukuda was committed to China-Japan friendship and upheld correct views of history. During his tenure he signed the fourth political document between China and Japan. Xi expressed hope that Fukuda's family would carry on his legacy.
items.title: Xi Jinping Extends Condolences Over Death of Japan's Former PM Fukuda

items.summary: The bereaved family of Murat Cicek, a Kurdish man who died in custody at a Tokyo police station on July 2, has sued the Tokyo Metropolitan Government and his contract doctor. Filed Tuesday with the Tokyo District Court, the suit seeks ¥57 million ($361,000) in damages. The complaint alleges the doctor overlooked a bowel injury and that staff left him untreated despite symptoms.
items.title: Kurdish Man's Family Sues Tokyo Government Over Custody Death

items.summary: A government wildlife rescue center in Khon Kaen, Thailand reports annual leopard cat admissions rising from about 10 cats per year before 2023 to as many as 65 now. Staff treat burns and infections before rehabilitating kittens over two months for soft release into Phu Pha Man National Park. Mortality rates dropped to around 33% in 2026, from 60% previously. Local forests are nearing capacity, prompting studies of other areas.
items.title: Thai Center Rescues Injured Leopard Cat Cubs

items.summary: At the 2026 Financial Street Forum in Beijing, global asset managers said debate over Chinese assets has shifted from whether to allocate to how to allocate well. Regulators pledged broader and more predictable market opening. At a CSRC roundtable on Oct. 21, executives from GIC, Amundi, Allianz Global Investors and JP Morgan Asset Management discussed long-term opportunities amid geopolitical conflict, technological change and climate concerns. Michael Krautzberger of Allianz called China the closest rival to the US in AI. Li Yimei of China Asset Management stayed bullish over three pillars. Travis Spence highlighted Chinese bonds as a portfolio stabilizer. According to CSRC data, Chinese listed companies posted revenues of 37.7 trillion yuan ($5.65 trillion) and net profits of 3.6 trillion yuan, up 19.5% year-on-year in the first half of the year, with dividends and buybacks totaling 2.1 trillion yuan. Participants said global capital is entering a new phase of systematic re-pricing of Chinese assets.
items.title: Global Asset Managers Recalibrate China Allocation at Beijing Forum

items.summary: Tayla Lee Brailey, a former high school teacher in Sydney, was sentenced to 15 months in prison after pleading guilty to four charges relating to sexual offences against two teenage students in 2024. Judge Elizabeth Ryan said the breach of trust warranted custody and ordered her onto the NSW Police child protection register for 15 years.
items.title: Former Sydney teacher jailed for sex acts with students

items.summary: Football Australia says it is monitoring security in the Middle East ahead of two Socceroos friendlies, one against Qatar in Doha and another against Jordan in Amman. The matches are scheduled next month as final warm-ups before January's Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia. Recent regional violence has raised concerns, but FA says it expects the games to go ahead.
items.title: Football Australia expects Middle East friendlies to proceed

items.summary: Asian tech shares rose on SK hynix's blockbuster third-quarter results, with operating profit up 632% to US$62. 8bn (€54. 2bn), the firm said Wednesday after six straight records of strong revenue and profit from advanced semiconductor demand. The gain added to AI optimism following Anthropic's IPO filing showing about 1,300% first-half revenue growth and a reported US$63bn financing structure for new capacity announced Tuesday by Broadcom with Citi, Blackstone and Morgan Stanley. SK hynix shares climbed almost 9%, while South Korean rival Samsung added more than 8%.
items.title: SK hynix profit surge lifts Asian tech stocks amid AI optimism

items.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy revealed on Tuesday that Ukrainian forces, in an operation codenamed Veles carried out by the National Guard's 2nd Khartiia Corps near Kupiansk, infiltrated Russian positions through underground gas pipelines. He said more than 100 Russian troops had been eliminated and over 30 captured. Zelenskyy described transforming a tactic previously used against Ukraine.
items.title: Ukraine's Underground Pipeline Operation Near Kupiansk

items.summary: The United States says it will issue visas to Flávio Bolsonaro and his family, even as reports say he may have left Brazil after losing the presidential election by more than four million votes. His whereabouts are not independently confirmed. He lost to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva while refusing to concede.
items.title: U.S. To Issue Visas to Flávio Bolsonaro Amid Unclear Whereabouts

items.summary: South Korea has completed development of a domestically produced marine attack helicopter under a project costing about 450 billion won, roughly $337 million. The aircraft is based on the KUH-1 Surion platform and adds air-to-ground missiles plus systems to counter enemy helicopters and drones. It passed combat suitability evaluation in July and received airworthiness certification in August. Local media reported that production of around 20 helicopters will begin in 2027, according to DAPA.
items.title: South Korea Finishes Indigenous Marine Attack Helicopter Development

items.summary: As nearly 42% of votes were counted, Netanyahu's bloc was projected to win 57 seats—four short of the 61 needed for a majority. The opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot was expected to take 47 seats, while Arab parties could hold balance with 16. Figures remain provisional and may change as counting continues, per The Times of Israel citing the Central Elections Committee.
items.title: Netanyahu Bloc Falls Short of Majority in Israeli Vote Count

items.summary: A ceasefire that began in Oleshky has been extended across the wider Kherson region, according to sources who helped broker it. US First Lady Melania Trump said on Tuesday that the area had expanded to provide safe passage for humanitarian convoys, a claim later corroborated by Ukraine's public ombudsman press secretary and deputy head of Kherson Oleksandr Tolokonnikov. The truce will be followed by aid deliveries and an evacuation planned for Friday. Residents report severe hunger amid no food or electricity since the 2023 Kakhovka Dam breach, while escape routes remain mined. Ukrainian officials warn evacuees may end up in Russia rather than Ukraine.
items.title: Ceasefire Extended Across Kherson Region for Humanitarian Aid

items.summary: Marry Mubaiwa, the former wife of Zimbabwe's vice-president Constantino Chiwenga, was released from remand after about seven years while her husband faced an attempted murder trial. Charged in 2019 over claims she tried to impede his medical treatment in South Africa, she had been denied bail and suffered prejudice during proceedings. A magistrate ordered the release citing mental, physical and financial harm; the state sought a one-month postponement to engage witnesses.
items.title: Ex-wife of Zimbabwe's vice-president freed after seven years on remand

items.summary: The Information reported Tuesday that OpenAI is planning to buy Google's AI chips, citing a person familiar with the matter. The report disclosed no financial terms or details. It would deepen ties between the two rivals despite competing in AI products and search. Both companies declined comment; Google did not respond outside business hours.
items.title: OpenAI reportedly plans purchase of Google AI chips amid surging demand

items.summary: Excess funds with Indian lenders fell from a September high of 11 trillion rupees ($116 billion) to 462 billion rupees by Oct. 26, per a Bloomberg Economics index, amid RBI measures defending the rupee at a near-record low. Analysts at IDFC First Bank and Emkay Global Financial Services expect tightness to persist as liquidity replenishment stays limited. Certificate of deposit rates rose about 40-50 basis points last week to a seven-month high.
items.title: RBI tightens liquidity as rupee nears record low, draining lender reserves

items.summary: Anthropic, the maker of Claude, filed to go public in the US. The article highlights four Indian-origin executives: CFO and CTO Krishna Rao, Claude Code co-creator Rahul Patil, Sid Bidasaria, and Neil Buddy Shah, who chairs its Long-Term Benefit Trust. Anthropic reported $16.3 billion in first-half 2026 revenue versus $1.16 billion a year earlier, though net loss widened to $80.7 billion while operating loss narrowed to $693 million from $2.1 billion.
items.title: Anthropic Files for US IPO as Four Indian-Origin Executives Take Center Stage

items.summary: Anthropic published its IPO prospectus, which Finshots summarised for readers. The company earns money through usage-based payments and subscriptions; in FY25 it made $4.5 billion in revenue, over 1,000% more than the previous year, rising to $16 billion in the first half of FY26, up around 1,300%. Roughly 80% comes from usage-based payments and 20% from subscriptions. Despite this growth, Anthropic posted an operating loss of $8 billion and a net loss of $41 billion in FY25; its operating loss narrowed to $693 million but the net loss reached $80 billion in the first half of FY26, partly due to a $72 billion accounting adjustment. Finshots notes that underlying operating economics appear improving while risks include limited shareholder control and revenue concentration.
items.title: Finshots Breaks Down Anthropic’s IPO Prospectus

items.summary: A joint Bihar and Andhra Pradesh police team arrested two youths, Aditya Pandey (23) and Raja Kumar (24), at the Indo-Nepal border town of Raxaul for allegedly relaying One-Time Passwords to Pakistani intelligence operatives. SDPO Manish Anand led the raid that seized two phones with forensic evidence linking suspects to money transfers tied to Case No. 0-01/2026, from which Vijayawada investigators arrived on October 25 after tracking digital footprints.
items.title: Bihar and Andhra Police Arrest Two in Raxaul Over WhatsApp Espionage Ring

items.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to roughly 60,000 employees across the US, Canada, the UK and India at level 70 and below. Chief people officer Amy Coleman announced the Voluntary Exit Offer in a Monday memo, with no age or tenure requirement and decisions due by early December. Eligibility rests on team participation rather than individual choice; AI, Copilot, Windows, Xbox, finance and HR teams qualify fully, while sales, marketing and security do not. Accepting employees exit at year's end for up to 39 weeks of salary plus stock vesting and career support, but without the extended healthcare in the spring program. This is Microsoft's second buyout of 2026 following layoffs that cut about 4,800 jobs in July alone. The company says it expects fewer takers than the earlier retirement offer and insists this does not signal further job cuts, though a spokesperson noted future offers may follow business need.
items.title: Microsoft Extends Voluntary Exit Offer to Indian Staff

items.summary: Google began rolling out a built-in audio recorder in the Gemini Notebook mobile app on Android and iOS, starting October 27. Recordings last up to one hour and are stored as transcripts that become queryable sources within a notebook. Google first announced the feature on September 15. Creators Toolbox summarized details from Google's help center, noting no required plan or language limit is stated.
items.title: Google Rolls Out One-Hour Audio Recording in Gemini Notebook

items.summary: Google DeepMind released Genie 4 in research preview, describing it as its most realistic and interactive world model yet. The system generates photorealistic worlds with built-in audio—music, ambient sounds and dialogue—and lets users change scenes live via text or image prompts. Built on Gemini Omni, a scene stays consistent for up to two minutes. It is available now to trusted testers through Project Genie but remains closed to the public.
items.title: Google DeepMind Releases Real-Time AI World Model Genie 4

items.summary: Former Supreme Court judge Sanjay Kishan Kaul said pre-trial detention has become 'punishment' in India, commenting on bail denials to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam. He argued that prolonged proceedings can punish people before conviction or acquittal, and that bail should generally be the norm.
items.title: Ex-SC Judge Kaul Calls Pre-Trial Detention a Punishment in India's System

items.summary: BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal are in advanced negotiations to revive their alliance ahead of the Punjab assembly elections, though seat-sharing and accommodating rebel faction Punar Surjit remain unresolved. The parties' equation has shifted after SAD's decline since 2020 and BJP's gains; sources say BJP's share could nearly double from its usual 23 seats in the 117-member House. Home Minister Amit Shah says the NDA will win, while Badal signals openness to other partners. The alliance is seen as their best shot at power amid rising Hindu-Sikh harmony concerns and Waris Punjab De's challenge.
items.title: BJP and Akali Dal Resume Seat-Sharing Talks Before Punjab Polls

items.summary: Residents of the Villa Vie Odyssey, a cruise ship stranded without fuel off Sihanoukville after running out of diesel during an around-the-world voyage that began in October 2024, were ordered to disembark by 2 p.m. on Tuesday, villa owner Mikael Petterson said. About 200 residents remained aboard the 650-passenger vessel when the order came. Villa Vie Residences says fuel costs have risen sharply since the Iran War began and is seeking new funding within 60 days while covering lodging but not travel out of Cambodia.
items.title: Villa Vie Odyssey Residents Ordered Off Stranded Cruise Ship in Cambodia

items.summary: Jio Platforms shares jumped 21% on their Mumbai debut, valuing the company at $108.3 billion and marking Reliance Industries’ first listing in two decades. The stock opened at 1,358 rupees a share versus its 1,119-rupee offer price. Jio’s telecoms business serves more than 530 million customers. Brokerages called the valuation attractive but flagged competition and regulatory changes as risks.
items.title: Jio Lists at Record $3.2 Billion in India IPO

items.summary: Exit polls from Israel’s election, reported by Al Jazeera, showed a neck-and-neck race between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and rival Gadi Eisenkot. Neither bloc was projected to win the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member Knesset; Arab-led parties were expected to take 18 seats. Final results are due Friday.
items.title: Israel Exit Polls Show Netanyahu Bloc Neck-and-Neck With Rivals

items.summary: Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated that India's mobile phone manufacturing sector generated Rs 25,000 crore in direct tax collections, exceeding the Rs 19,000 crore paid out under its production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme. He added the programme contributed Rs 3,000 crore in GST and said electronics manufacturing employs 25 Lakh people while mobile manufacturing alone employs 12 Lakh. Vaishnaw dismissed reports questioning the model as he pushed for a new Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme approved by the Union Cabinet in July with Rs 62,500 crore allocated to run from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31.
items.title: Vaishnaw Defends Mobile PLI Scheme on Tax and Jobs Grounds

items.summary: The BJP won four of the six counted seats in Uttar Pradesh’s Legislative Council election, while the Samajwadi Party (SP) took one. The ruling party led in Gorakhpur Teacher and Agra Graduate; the SP was ahead across Varanasi Graduate, Agra Teacher, Lucknow Graduate and Jhansi Graduate. Counting for six remaining seats continued on Wednesday under single transferable vote procedures that began Tuesday at 8am. An Opposition candidate boycotted counting in Gorakhpur over alleged irregularities, saying votes suddenly swung to the BJP rival by about 450 votes. The SP had won three of 11 council seats in 2020, when the BJP held six and independents two. Congress-SP alliance later polled 43.52% of votes for its 43 assembly seats in 2024.
items.title: BJP and SP split Uttar Pradesh council seats as counting drags on

items.summary: According to StockEdge's technical scan data, seven stocks in the Nifty200 index had closing prices that crossed above their 200-day moving averages on October 27, 2026. The 200-day moving average is a widely used indicator for gauging overall trend direction; when a stock's price stays above it on the daily timeframe, it typically signals an uptrend.
items.title: Seven Nifty200 Stocks Cross Above Their 200-Day Moving Averages

items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government announced a revision of auto-rickshaw fares, doubling the minimum base fare from 25 rupees to 50 rupees for the first 1.8 kilometres and raising the per-kilometre rate from 12 rupees to 25 rupees. The change follows long-standing demands and multiple protests by the Auto Drivers Association after more than a decade of campaigning.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Doubles Auto-Rickshaw Minimum Fare Amid Cyclone Michaung

items.summary: India reportedly invited Pakistan's Heritage and Culture Minister Aurangzeb Khan Khichi to the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum, set for New Delhi from November 20 to 22. All ten member states were extended invitations by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, who announced the event in Dushanbe on October 20 amid ongoing India-Pakistan tensions following Operation Sindoor in May 2025.
items.title: India Extends SCO Civilisation Forum Invitation to Pakistan

items.summary: Videos show waves breaching the coast and trees uprooted as cyclonic storm Arnab hit Odisha and Andhra Pradesh. The India Meteorological Department said the powerful 'very severe' storm remained practically stationary along the Andhra Pradesh coast after its northern spiral band moved inland, bringing heavy rain, strong winds and flooding to districts across both states.
items.title: Cyclone Arnab Lashes Odisha and Andhra with Waves, Uprooted Trees

items.summary: In Karnataka's four-seat Legislative Council poll, the BJP-JD(S) opposition alliance won all seats: JD(S) took Bengaluru Teachers' Constituency from Congress via A P Ranganath by 908 votes (10,810 to 9,902), while BJP held its three segments. The outcome was seen as a sign of opposition consolidation and not expected to affect the Congress government's stability.
items.title: Opposition Alliance Sweeps Karnataka Legislative Council MLC Polls

items.summary: Stock market benchmarks Sensex and Nifty tumbled in early trade on Wednesday, dragged by IT companies, rising crude oil prices and caution ahead of the US Federal Reserve's policy decision. The 30-share BSE Sensex dropped 601.14 points to 72,997.55; the 50-share NSE Nifty fell 146 points to 22,604.80. Brent crude traded higher at USD 115.4 a barrel.
items.title: Indian benchmark indices fell sharply on Wednesday amid rising crude prices

items.summary: The proposal to extend Bengaluru’s Namma Metro Yellow Line from Bommasandra in Karnataka to Hosur in Tamil Nadu has drawn strong public support, according to a ground report by The Federal Karnataka. IT employees, students and auto drivers say the line would ease severe traffic congestion along stretches such as Attibele and Electronic City. In 2023, Karnataka’s IT and Biotechnology Minister Priyank Kharge raised objections that lower costs in Hosur could lure Bengaluru industries across the border; however, some industry associations did not share those concerns. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay appealed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for approval. The estimated cost is around Rs 6,900 crore, and final clearance still depends on several factors.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister appeals for Bengaluru-Hosur Metro extension

items.summary: India has invited all ten SCO member states, including Pakistan, to its inaugural Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi from November 20-22. Officials said the multilateral invite is unrelated to bilateral ties but should be read within broader SCO collaboration. The forum was proposed by PM Modi at the Tianjin summit and organised by India's Culture and External Affairs ministries.
items.title: Will Pakistan's minister visit Delhi? India invites Islamabad first time after Operation Sindoor

items.summary: Shaktikanta Das, RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta, said India is in striking distance of 8% growth. He cited macroeconomic stability, continuing structural reforms, and strategic policy initiatives developing domestic capacity as the triple engines powering it. Das highlighted the BFSI sector's role in supporting next-gen Digital Public Infrastructure, green finance, and financial inclusion on the path to a high-income economy.
items.title: RBI's Shaktikanta Das sees India near 8% growth on reforms and stability
